parsed.explanation: The division is strongly protective in daily life: public-accommodations law covers gender identity, hate-crime law covers it, single-user bathrooms must be gender-neutral, shield laws protect gender-affirming care, and there is no local bathroom ban or care ban for minors. But the national layer controls entry documents, federal facilities, federal custody and federal investigations. A trans visitor is exposed at the border to sex-mismatch refusal, additional evidence demands, and possible lifetime fraud ineligibility; federal facilities exclude by birth sex; immigration custody has documented severe abuse. These federal universal-exposure features are not cancelled by division law. A family with a minor also faces federal care-investigation and records exposure. No criminalisation of trans identity or execution pathway is documented, so this is low Elevated Risk, not Severe.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex-binary document policy; new X markers stopped; entry cable requires refusal or additional evidence on sex discrepancy; suspected material misrepresentation can yield lifetime fraud ineligibility; trans-athlete entry ban; reports of confiscated or blocked passports and stranded travellers.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; passport policy is challenged in court; some related orders are enjoined. Division public-accommodation law does not reach border screening.
entry_documents.interaction: A visitor arrives on a home passport, but national officers screen sex, appearance and name mismatch before any division protection applies; refusal or secondary detention is a federal-stage event.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports trans men subjected to forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse; corrections policies remove hormones, cut hair and substitute psychiatric treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented for national immigration or corrections custody. Division shield and nondiscrimination laws do not bind national custody.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A border document discrepancy can move the traveller into national secondary inspection or detention, where division protections are unavailable.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities matching identity; federal buildings and airports remain covered. Some states criminalise bathroom use, but not this division.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Division requires gender-neutral single-user public bathrooms and bans gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations; no division bathroom ban.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private hotels, restaurants and division buildings are broadly protected; federal facilities and transit remain under the national exclusion.

care_services.exposure: National executive order frames minor gender-affirming care as mutilation; national justice department subpoenas hospital records of patients under 19; proposed rule would bar public insurance reimbursement for minors; providers face hostile climate.
care_services.protection: Division shield laws enacted in 2023 and 2024 are enforceable against out-of-state action; insurance coverage for transgender care since 2013; conversion-therapy ban; no division care ban for minors.
care_services.interaction: Adult care in the division is strongly protected; a travelling minor or family still faces national investigative and records exposure that the division shield does not clearly cancel.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent groups; a national reward system and 'radical gender ideology' language create official threat framing.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Guidance says mere disagreement is not targeted; some orders are enjoined; division hate-crime law and panic-defence repeal protect local victims.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Raises scrutiny of activism and speech and may embolden hostility, but no general criminal ban on transgender status is documented; local police recourse exists in law but enforcement data are absent.

minors_guardians.exposure: National order directs investigation and prosecution of teachers who use preferred names or facilitate social transition; minor care is framed as abuse; hospital records are subpoenaed; national insurance rule targets minors.
minors_guardians.protection: Division anti-bullying law, 2023 school policy, conversion-therapy ban, shield law and absence of a division care ban.
minors_guardians.interaction: A family visiting the division gets local school and health protections, but national entry, investigative and custody authority follows the minor; care-seeking can trigger records exposure.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No transgender-specific violence rate or denominator is provided; national opinion supports sex-defined documents and sports restrictions; official hostility may increase social risk.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Division hate-crime law covers gender identity since 1999, panic defence was repealed in 2021, and public accommodations cover hotels and restaurants; no division enforcement data are given.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local incidents have a legal route; the national climate and missing enforcement data leave practical police response uncertain.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: National entry and custody decisions have no documented effective visitor remedy; a lifetime fraud finding is possible; passport policy is litigated but unresolved; division enforcement data are absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Division courts, public-accommodations law, hate-crime law and shield laws; national civil-liberties suit; some executive orders blocked or enjoined; legal-aid FAQ.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies operate for division-level daily life but not for national border, facility or custody exposures; which measures are in force at travel time controls.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia criminalises gender presentation and documents lethal custody with executions. This dossier documents no criminalisation of transgender identity, no execution pathway, and strong division nondiscrimination, so it is well above 0.15.

Vellandra routinely denies entry to visibly transgender visitors with no remedy. Here refusal and lifetime ineligibility are possible on document discrepancy, but not categorical, and daily life in the division is strongly protected. This is somewhat above 0.35, not below.

Kestrel Isles uses secondary screening and administrative refusal with some appeal. Here national entry can impose a lifetime fraud bar and custody abuse is documented, but division public-accommodations and shield protections are much stronger than Kestrel's. The net is around low Elevated, similar to or slightly below 0.55.

Meridia has trained border officers, tribunal appeals and brief detention. This dossier has materially harsher national entry-document and custody exposures, despite strong division protections, so it is well below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: The operative system is split: division law makes hotels, restaurants, clinics, bathrooms and many services relatively safe for an outed transgender visitor, and division hate-crime and shield laws provide real local recourse. National authority nevertheless controls the border, federal buildings, federal custody and federal investigations. The sharpest documented exposures are universal national document screening with possible refusal or lifetime ineligibility, federal facility exclusion by birth sex, and severe harm in immigration custody. A lone adult faces these mainly at entry and in federal spaces; a family with a minor also faces national care-investigation and records exposure. Because no criminalisation of transgender status or execution pathway is documented, and division protections are unusually strong, the rating sits at the low end of Elevated Risk rather than Severe Risk.
